items.title: Post #5 — Generosity scattered, five fault lines
items.copy: giving is down is the wrong headline, generosity didn't shrink it scattered, dollars up base changed fewer people giving more, five fault lines ROI privacy anonymity frustration access, donor-advised funds never show up in your file, donor behavior trends

items.title: Post #22 — Donors left because they stopped feeling seen
items.copy: donors didn't leave because they ran out of money they stopped feeling seen, lapsed donor filed under math, felt like an ATM only mail was another ask nobody told them what their gift did, 70% of first-time donors never give a second gift 2% of lapsed donors come back Fundraising Effectiveness Project, every touchpoint builds or burns the relationship, donor retention stewardship

items.title: Post #10 — I stayed off LinkedIn for two years
items.copy: stayed off LinkedIn two years on purpose, when the CEO's voice is loudest everybody else's gets quieter, wanted my team's names on the ideas, switched my voice back on in April, when you step back people step up, the work needs you less than your ego hopes, 75% of B2B decision-makers thought leadership Edelman 60% pay a premium, CEO leadership thought leadership

items.title: Post #12 — A room where leaders got to take
items.copy: nonprofit leaders spend careers saying give, at our CONVERGE summit a room of them got to take, nobody wanted anything from them, running on empty out loud, being the guest after a career of hosting, 89% of nonprofit CEOs worried about burnout CEP State of Nonprofits, you can't pour from empty

items.title: Post #9 — The load, by the numbers
items.copy: every leader at CONVERGE carrying more than a year ago, CEP State of Nonprofits 89% of nonprofit CEOs worried about burnout 46% very much nearly double, 1 in 4 burnout hitting staff up from 17%, 73% higher demand for services, the load you're feeling is measurable, saying it out loud is part of leading through it, nonprofit leadership burnout
